# AirSQL

> AirSQL is a free, open-source Mac app (macOS 13.1 or later, Apple silicon and Intel) for MySQL and MariaDB: connections direct or through SSH tunnels, jump hosts and proxies, a SQL console, a data grid with safe editing, schema tools, client tools (mysql, mysqldump), compare and reconcile, and access for AI agents over MCP at the level the person at the Mac sets for each connection. Nothing is written to a server without the person's Run, Apply or approval, and agents never see saved passwords.

- Install: `brew install --cask kleash/tap/airsql` (or the zip from https://github.com/kleash/airsql/releases).

## AirSQL Help
- [Home](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/): AirSQL is a Mac app for MySQL and MariaDB. It is in development: these pages grow with it.
- [Install AirSQL](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/install.html): AirSQL needs macOS 13.1 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. It is free, and it needs no account.
- [Getting started](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/getting-started.html)
- [Settings](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/settings.html): Open **AirSQL ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). Changes are saved as you make them.
- [Check SQL before it runs](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/sql-preview.html): Some changes show their SQL in a sheet before anything runs: applying edits in a table, changing a table's structure, dropping or renaming, restoring a dump, and sync scripts.
- [Trust a server](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/trust-a-server.html): When a server's certificate isn't one macOS trusts (it is self-signed, or from your company's own certificate authority), AirSQL shows its SHA-256 fingerprint and asks before connecting.
- [SQL log](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/sql-log.html): AirSQL writes every statement it sends to a server into one file on your Mac, just before the statement goes out. Use it to see exactly what AirSQL did: what the console ran, what a table edit applied, what the navigator asked the server for.
- [Read-only queries](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/read-only-queries.html): Where only reading is allowed, such as a query from an AI agent, AirSQL first checks that the statement can only read. The check is strict on purpose: when in doubt it refuses, and it says why in one line.
- [The SQL console](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/console.html): A console tab is where you write and run SQL on one connection. Its statements run one at a time, on the connection's own session, which every console tab of that connection shares.
- [Connections and routes](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/connections.html): A connection is a MySQL or MariaDB server AirSQL remembers: its address, the login, how to reach it (its route) and a few options. Passwords go in your Keychain, never in AirSQL's files.
- [Browse a server](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/navigator.html): Once a connection is connected, the sidebar shows its databases under it. Each database groups its objects by kind: tables, views, sequences (MariaDB), procedures, functions, triggers and events, with how many there are.
- [Change tables, views and routines](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/editors.html): AirSQL edits a table's structure in a form, and views, procedures, functions, triggers and events as the CREATE statement that makes them. Nothing changes on the server until you apply, and the SQL that will run is always shown first.
- [Export, restore, copy and import](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/client-tools.html): AirSQL backs up and moves data with your own `mysqldump` and `mysql` (or MariaDB's `mariadb-dump` and `mariadb`) when you have them, and with its own code when you don't. Every command here is in the **Tools** and **File** menus and in a connection's right-click menu in the sidebar.
- [Compare two databases](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/compare.html): **Tools ▸ Compare…** (or **Compare…** in a connection's or a database's menu, which starts from it) opens a window that compares two databases, on the same server or on two different connections, such as production against staging or MySQL 8 against MariaDB. A connection that isn't connected connects when you choose it, asking for a password or to trust a certificate on the compare window as the main window would; each side then works through its own route, on a session of its own. The compare only reads; nothing changes until you run the sync script yourself.
- [AI agents](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/agents.html): Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients can use AirSQL to read your schemas, run read-only queries, profile tables and propose SQL for you to run. They work through AirSQL on your Mac, so they see only what you allow, never your passwords, and can't change data.
- [Liquibase changelogs](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/liquibase.html): AirSQL writes [Liquibase](https://www.liquibase.com) changelogs in Liquibase's **formatted SQL**: plain SQL with `--changeset author:id` lines, which Liquibase reads as it is. You can write one of a whole database, save a compare's sync script as changesets, or save any change AirSQL shows you before it runs. AirSQL only writes the files: run them with your own `liquibase` (`liquibase update`, `liquibase rollback-count 1`…).
- [A table's rows](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/table-data.html): A table tab shows a table's or view's rows in the data grid. They load a page at a time from the connection's data session, a session of their own, so a long query in a console never holds them up. Edits wait until you apply them.
- [Read the data in a grid](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/data-grid.html): A table's rows and a console's results show in the same grid. These parts of it help you read what is there: the status bar's figures, the value panel, Record View, Transpose, other ways to show a column, colours, text, charts, and a column's summary. Loading, filtering, editing, copying and exporting a table's rows are on [A table's rows](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/table-data.html).
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/shortcuts.html): Every command is in the menu bar, with its shortcut next to it, and right-click menus show the same commands. Hold the pointer over a menu item to see what it does. A greyed-out item says why it is off.
- [Privacy and security](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/privacy-security.html): AirSQL holds the keys to your databases, so it is careful by default: it talks only to the servers you set up, your passwords stay in your Keychain, and nothing changes on a server until you say so.
- [Troubleshooting](https://kleash.github.io/airsql/troubleshooting.html): AirSQL says what went wrong in plain words, with the server's own error under **Details**. Here is what to do about the common problems.
